args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
(Counterparty Draft → Firm/Secured Party Required Form)

Document: Account Control Agreement (Deposit Account)
Parties: [Debtor/Company] ("Company"); [Secured Party/Administrative Agent] ("Secured Party"); [Depository Bank] ("Bank")
Related Facility: Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated as of [Closing Date] (as amended, the "Credit Agreement")
Accounts: See Schedule I (Account Details)
Base references: Internal ACA Playbook (Lender/Secured-Party form); executed Credit Agreement; Bank standard control agreement form; Exhibit B (Survival Matrix); Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Deal Team Correspondence (controlling instruction)
Markup source: Counterparty revision of Bank/Company paper
Legend: [DELETE: text to be deleted]  [INSERT: text to be inserted]  [MOVE]  Comments in braces {Comment: …}

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PREAMBLE / RECITALS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of [Effective Date] by and among [Company legal name], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Company"), [Secured Party / Administrative Agent name], as [Administrative Agent / Collateral Agent] for the benefit of the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement (in such capacity, the "Secured Party"), and [Depository Bank legal name] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

A. The Company and the lenders party thereto have entered into that certain Credit Agreement dated as of [Closing Date] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement"), pursuant to which the Secured Party and the other Secured Parties have agreed to extend credit to the Company on the terms set forth therein.

B. The Company has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Accounts described on Schedule I hereto (each, an "Account" and collectively, the "Accounts") pursuant to the Security Agreement and the other Collateral Documents.

C. The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Accounts by "control" under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the "UCC"), and to set forth the Bank's agreement to comply with instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent by the Company.

{Comment: Retain standard control-perfection recital; do not dilute "without further consent" language per playbook §2.1 and Credit Agreement §[Collateral/Control] requirements.}

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 1.1 Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement. As used herein:

"Account" and "Accounts" have the meanings set forth in the Recitals and Schedule I.

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York [INSERT: or the city in which the Bank's office maintaining the Accounts is located] are authorized or required by law to close.

"Control Notice" [INSERT: or "Notice of Exclusive Control"] means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Accounts.

"Indemnified Person" means the Bank, the Secured Party and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents and affiliates.

"Instructions" means instructions originated by the Secured Party directing the disposition of funds in an Account, including a Control Notice.

"Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities (actual or contingent), operations, condition (financial or otherwise) or prospects of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, (b) the ability of the Company to perform its obligations under this Agreement, the Credit Agreement or any other Loan Document, (c) the legality, validity, binding effect or enforceability against the Company of this Agreement or any other Loan Document, or (d) the rights and remedies of the Secured Party or the Bank under this Agreement or any other Loan Document[, including the validity, perfection or priority of any Lien granted hereunder or under the Collateral Documents].

[DELETE: ; provided, however, that "Material Adverse Effect" shall exclude any effect arising from or relating to (i) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination or proceeding by any Governmental Authority, (ii) any change in law, regulation or regulatory policy (including banking, deposit-insurance or sanctions rules), or (iii) the public announcement or pendency of any of the foregoing.]

{Comment: REJECT counterparty MAE regulatory carve-outs in full. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect precisely these carve-outs. Playbook requires MAE to preserve regulatory/enforcement risk; Credit Agreement MAE has no such carve-out. Reversion is mandatory.}

"Officer's Certificate" means a certificate signed by a Responsible Officer of the Company.

"Secured Obligations" means all Obligations under the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents.

"Survival Period" has the meaning set forth in Section 8.3 [INSERT: and Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)].

{Comment: Cross-reference Exhibit B survival matrix; counterparty limitation-period change is rejected as walk-away per controlling deal correspondence.}

Section 1.2 UCC Terms. "Deposit account," "control," "entitlement order," and other UCC terms have the meanings given in the UCC.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE II — THE ACCOUNTS; ESTABLISHMENT OF CONTROL
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 2.1 Identification of Accounts. The Bank maintains the Accounts for the Company as set forth on Schedule I. The Company represents that Schedule I is complete and accurate as of the date hereof [INSERT: and covenants to update Schedule I within three (3) Business Days of any change in account number, title, location or jurisdiction].

Section 2.2 Control. The Bank agrees that it will comply with Instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of the funds in each Account without further consent by the Company. The Bank shall not comply with instructions concerning any Account originated by the Company or any other person other than the Secured Party after the Bank's receipt of a Control Notice, except as expressly permitted in Section 2.4 pending effectiveness of exclusive control [INSERT: or as otherwise agreed in writing by the Secured Party].

{Comment: Playbook §2.1 / Bank form §2 — irrevocable agreement to comply with Secured Party instructions is non-negotiable for UCC §9-104 control.}

Section 2.3 Priority of Secured Party's Interest. The Bank subordinates any security interest, lien or right of setoff it may have in or against the Accounts [INSERT: or any funds therein] to the security interest of the Secured Party, except for the Bank's rights under Section 5.1 (fees, returned items, chargebacks and overdrafts) as expressly limited herein. [INSERT: The Bank represents that it has not entered into, and covenants that it will not enter into, any other control agreement or similar arrangement with respect to any Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.]

Section 2.4 Interim Operation; Control Notice.
(a) Until the Bank receives a Control Notice, the Company may operate the Accounts and the Bank may honor instructions from the Company in the ordinary course, subject to this Agreement and applicable law.
(b) Upon the Bank's receipt of a Control Notice, the Bank shall (i) immediately cease complying with Company instructions as to the Accounts, (ii) comply solely with Instructions of the Secured Party, and (iii) [INSERT: within one (1) Business Day] confirm in writing to the Secured Party receipt of the Control Notice and the available balance of each Account.
(c) [INSERT: The Bank shall not require any further authentication, indemnity or documentation from the Secured Party as a condition to complying with a Control Notice other than commercially reasonable verification that the notice purports to be from the Secured Party in accordance with Section 7.2.]

{Comment: Insert tight confirmation timing and bar on extra conditions to honor NEOC — common Bank-form pushback; playbook requires Secured Party-friendly mechanics.}

Section 2.5 No Other Accounts; Location. The Company shall not maintain deposit accounts constituting Collateral other than the Accounts and Excluded Accounts permitted under the Credit Agreement. Each Account is and shall remain a "deposit account" under UCC §9-102. [INSERT: No Account shall be relocated to a branch or office outside the United States without prior written consent of the Secured Party.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE III — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 3.1 Company Representations. The Company represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank that:
(a) it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization;
(b) it has full power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement;
(c) this Agreement constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms;
(d) the execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with its organizational documents, any material agreement or any law or order applicable to it;
(e) it is the sole account holder of each Account, and no other person has any interest in any Account except the Secured Party and permitted Bank rights hereunder;
(f) Schedule I correctly identifies each Account; and
(g) [INSERT: except as set forth on Schedule 3.7, there is no pending or, to the Company's knowledge, threatened regulatory action, inquiry, investigation or proceeding by any Governmental Authority that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect any Account, the Bank's ability to comply with Instructions, or the Secured Party's control or Lien.]

{Comment: INSERT regulatory representation expressly tied to Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries). Counterparty MAE carve-out attempted to neutralize this risk; representation + schedule disclosure is the correct construct. Scheduled exceptions control.}

Section 3.2 Bank Representations. The Bank represents and warrants that:
(a) it is a [bank / national banking association] duly organized and validly existing;
(b) the Accounts are maintained as deposit accounts on its books;
(c) it has not entered into any currently effective agreement with any third party to comply with instructions concerning any Account originated by a person other than the Company or the Secured Party; and
(d) this Agreement has been duly authorized and constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation.

Section 3.3 Secured Party Representations. The Secured Party represents that it is authorized under the Credit Agreement and Collateral Documents to enter into this Agreement and to issue Instructions and Control Notices.

[DELETE any counterparty-added "knowledge" qualifiers or materiality scrapes on Sections 3.1(e)–(g) and 3.2(c) beyond playbook baselines.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE IV — COVENANTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 4.1 Company Covenants. The Company shall:
(a) maintain each Account as a deposit account subject to this Agreement;
(b) not permit any Account to become subject to any other control agreement or competing Lien, except as expressly permitted by the Credit Agreement;
(c) provide the Secured Party and the Bank with prompt written notice of any change to Schedule I information [INSERT: and of any regulatory action of the type described in Section 3.1(g)];
(d) not close any Account without prior written consent of the Secured Party [INSERT: (and simultaneous opening of a replacement Account subject to an account control agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party)]; and
(e) comply with all terms of the Credit Agreement relating to Cash Management and Collateral Accounts.

Section 4.2 Bank Covenants. The Bank shall:
(a) maintain the Accounts in accordance with this Agreement and its standard account documentation to the extent not inconsistent herewith (this Agreement controls in the event of conflict as to control, priority, setoff subordination and Instructions);
(b) [INSERT: provide the Secured Party, upon request and at the Company's expense, with copies of account statements and available balance information for the Accounts;]
(c) promptly notify the Secured Party if the Bank receives notice of any levy, attachment, garnishment or competing claim against any Account; and
(d) not amend its account documentation in a manner that adversely affects the Secured Party's rights hereunder without prior written notice to the Secured Party [INSERT: and, if material to control or priority, prior written consent].

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE V — BANK FEES, SETOFF, RETURNED ITEMS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 5.1 Bank's Limited Recourse. The Bank may charge the Accounts for its customary fees and charges, and for returned items, chargebacks, overdrafts and account losses related to the Accounts, [DELETE: and may exercise rights of setoff and recoupment against the Accounts for any obligations of the Company to the Bank, whether or not relating to the Accounts] [INSERT: provided that (i) such charges are limited to fees, returned items, chargebacks and overdrafts arising in respect of the Accounts, (ii) the Bank's right of setoff against the Accounts is limited to amounts owing solely in respect of the Accounts (and not unrelated credit exposures), and (iii) after receipt of a Control Notice, the Bank shall not exercise setoff without the prior written consent of the Secured Party except for returned items posted within [three (3)] Business Days after the Control Notice related to items deposited before the Control Notice].

{Comment: Playbook §5 — narrow Bank setoff; reject broad cross-affiliate / unrelated exposure setoff often in Bank paper.}

Section 5.2 Returned Items; Negative Balances. If an Account would be negative due to returned items or charges, the Company shall immediately deposit sufficient funds. [INSERT: The Secured Party shall have no liability for negative balances. Any retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 remain obligations of the Company and shall not be shifted to the Secured Party by operation of indemnification, setoff, or basket mechanics under this Agreement or any related agreement.]

{Comment: Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities — counterparty indemnification changes would silently shift these; insert express anti-shift protection.}

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE VI — INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 6.1 Company Indemnity. The Company agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless each Indemnified Person from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Accounts, or any action taken or omitted in accordance with this Agreement or Instructions, except to the extent resulting from the [DELETE: gross negligence or willful misconduct] [INSERT: gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad faith] of such Indemnified Person as determined by a final non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.

Section 6.2 Indemnification Cap.
[DELETE: The aggregate liability of the Company under Section 6.1 shall not exceed $[REDUCED CAP AMOUNT] (the "Indemnification Cap").]
[INSERT: The aggregate liability of the Company under Section 6.1 in respect of claims other than Excluded Cap Claims shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap set forth in the Credit Agreement indemnification and/or the amount equal to [playbook: not less than the aggregate principal amount of Secured Obligations / firm standard ACA cap aligned to Credit Agreement], provided that there shall be no cap on Excluded Cap Claims. "Excluded Cap Claims" means claims arising from (i) fraud, willful misconduct or bad faith of the Company, (ii) breach of the fundamental representations in Sections 3.1(e), 3.1(f) and 3.1(g) and corresponding covenants, (iii) failure to maintain exclusive Secured Party control once a Control Notice is effective, (iv) Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and any attempt to shift the same, and (v) third-party claims resulting from unauthorized disposition of Account funds contrary to Instructions.]

{Comment: REJECT silent reduction of indemnification cap. Restore Credit Agreement / playbook-aligned cap and uncapped buckets for fundamental control, fraud, and Schedule 5.2 items. Risk: High.}

Section 6.3 Basket.
[DELETE: No claim for indemnification under Section 6.1 may be made unless and until the aggregate amount of all claims exceeds $[BASKET], in which event the Company shall be liable for all claims including those comprising the basket (a "tipping basket").]
[INSERT: Subject to the client's conceded position on basket type: claims under Section 6.1 shall be subject to a tipping basket in the amount of $[BASKET AMOUNT] (the "Basket"), such that once aggregate indemnifiable losses exceed the Basket, the Company shall be liable for the full amount of such losses from the first dollar (tipping). The Basket shall not apply to Excluded Cap Claims or to claims under Sections 5.2, 6.5 or Article II control failures.]

{Comment: CONCEDE tipping basket conversion per controlling Deal Team Correspondence (client will concede basket conversion). Retain carve-outs so tipping basket cannot swallow control failures, fundamental reps, or Schedule 5.2 liabilities.}

Section 6.4 Bank Standard of Care; Limitation of Bank Liability. The Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted in good faith in accordance with this Agreement or Instructions believed by it to be genuine, except for its [INSERT: gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith]. [DELETE any counterparty attempt to impose a pure "ordinary care only" ceiling that eliminates gross negligence accountability where Bank form already accepts GN/WM.] IN NO EVENT SHALL THE BANK BE LIABLE FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, WHETHER OR NOT ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY THEREOF, EXCEPT TO THE EXTENT RESULTING FROM ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR BAD FAITH.

Section 6.5 Secured Party Reliance; No Secured Party Liability for Bank Acts. The Secured Party shall have no liability to the Company or the Bank for actions of the Bank, and may rely on account information and Bank confirmations without independent investigation. [INSERT: Nothing in this Article VI shall limit the Company's Obligations under the Credit Agreement or Collateral Documents.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE VII — NOTICES; INSTRUCTIONS; AUTHENTICATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 7.1 Notices. All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, or email (with confirmation) to the addresses set forth on Schedule II (or such other address as a party designates by notice). Notices are effective upon receipt (or refusal).

Section 7.2 Authentication of Instructions. The Bank may verify Instructions by callback or other commercially reasonable authentication procedures agreed with the Secured Party. [INSERT: Once authentication procedures are satisfied, the Bank shall promptly execute Instructions and shall not impose additional conditions inconsistent with Section 2.4(c).] The Bank may rely on communications purportedly from authorized persons designated on Schedule II.

Section 7.3 Electronic Transmission. Electronic signatures and PDF/email delivery are effective. [INSERT: Control Notices delivered by email to the Bank notice address on Schedule II are effective when received if sent from a designated Secured Party address.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE VIII — TERM; TERMINATION; SURVIVAL
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 8.1 Term. This Agreement remains in effect until terminated in accordance with this Article VIII.

Section 8.2 Termination.
(a) The Secured Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Bank and the Company upon payment in full of the Secured Obligations and termination of Commitments (or release of the Accounts as Collateral in accordance with the Credit Agreement).
(b) The Bank may terminate this Agreement upon [INSERT: not less than thirty (30) days'] prior written notice to the Company and the Secured Party, provided that no such termination shall be effective until the Accounts have been transferred to a successor depository bank and a replacement account control agreement reasonably satisfactory to the Secured Party is in full force and effect [INSERT: or the Secured Party has consented in writing to termination without replacement].
(c) The Company may not terminate this Agreement while any Secured Obligations remain outstanding without the Secured Party's prior written consent.

Section 8.3 Survival.

args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Matter: contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
To: Deal Team / Client
From: Contracts Counsel
Re: Deviations, Missing Protections, and Off-Market Terms in Counterparty Draft ACA
Related deliverable: aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline)

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement against (i) the firm's internal ACA playbook (secured-party form), (ii) the executed Credit Agreement and Collateral Documents, (iii) the depository bank's standard control agreement form, (iv) account details and disclosure schedules (including Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B Survival Matrix), and (v) deal-team correspondence. We disregarded misfiled unrelated administrative correspondence in the matter folder.

The counterparty accepts most firm-standard control mechanics but introduces three primary economic/risk deviations, each of which must be reconciled to the schedules:

1. Silent reduction of the indemnification cap, coupled with conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket — intersecting Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.
2. Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with regulatory-action carve-outs of exactly the kind implicated by Schedule 3.7's two pending regulatory inquiries.
3. A new contractual limitation period that shortens survival for core representations — contradicting Exhibit B and flagged by the client as a walk-away issue.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email): the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping) but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier contrary priority ordering in the thread is superseded.

Recommended posture: accept tipping basket with tight carve-outs; reject cap reduction and restore playbook/Credit Agreement-aligned cap with uncapped buckets; reject MAE regulatory carve-outs in full; reject survival shortening in full and reinstate Exhibit B. Implement all positions in aca-redline.docx.

II. CONTROLLING MATERIALS AND PRIORITY RULES

| Source | Role |
|---|---|
| Internal ACA Playbook | Baseline secured-party positions (control irrevocability, setoff narrow, NEOC mechanics, indemnity floors, NY law) |
| Executed Credit Agreement / Collateral Documents | Superior as between Company and Secured Party; MAE, Obligations, Cash Management, release mechanics |
| Bank standard form | Operational baseline for Bank duties; subordinate to ACA on control, priority, setoff, Instructions |
| Schedule 3.7 | Two pending regulatory inquiries — controls over general statements; intersects MAE carve-out fight |
| Schedule 5.2 | Retained liabilities — must not be silently shifted via cap/basket |
| Exhibit B Survival Matrix | Controls survival periods; contradicts counterparty limitation-period markup |
| Deal correspondence (latest) | Concede basket conversion; survival reduction = walk-away |
| Misfiled unrelated correspondence | IGNORE |

Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base contracts materials.

III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references (counterparty draft / redline): Article VI, Section 6.2 (Indemnification Cap); related Sections 6.1, 6.3, 5.2.

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
- ACA Company indemnity in favor of Bank and Secured Party Indemnified Persons should align to Credit Agreement indemnity economics or firm ACA floor.
- No silent reduction of cap below playbook/Credit Agreement level.
- Fundamental control failures, fraud/willful misconduct, and scheduled retained liabilities should be uncapped (Excluded Cap Claims).

Counterparty deviation:
- Cap amount is silently reduced below the negotiated/playbook level without express call-out in cover correspondence.
- No adequate uncapped buckets for control failures or Schedule 5.2 items.

Schedule interaction:
- Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift onto the Secured Party (or leave partially unrecoverable) if the reduced cap binds.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
- If a control failure, unauthorized disposition, or Schedule 5.2 retained item matures into loss, a reduced cap truncates recovery from the Company and may leave the Secured Party (or Bank, with downstream pressure on the facility) holding residual exposure.
- Silent reduction creates interpretive risk that the reduced figure was "agreed," complicating post-closing enforcement.
- Interaction with tipping basket (Issue 2) amplifies first-dollar exposure dynamics once the basket is exceeded, but still leaves quantum capped too low.

Recommended position:
- REJECT reduced cap.
- RESTORE Indemnification Cap to Credit Agreement / playbook-aligned level.
- INSERT "Excluded Cap Claims" uncapped: fraud/willful misconduct/bad faith; fundamental reps (sole account holder, Schedule I accuracy, no competing control agreement, Section 3.1(g) regulatory); failure to maintain exclusive control post-NEOC; Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; third-party claims from unauthorized disposition contrary to Instructions.
- Cross-provision: Section 5.2 express anti-shift language.

Redline treatment: DELETE reduced-cap sentence; INSERT restored cap + Excluded Cap Claims (see aca-redline.docx §6.2).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 2 — Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping Basket
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Article VI, Section 6.3 (Basket); interaction with §§6.1–6.2, 5.2.

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
- Firm baseline often prefers deductible (excess-only) basket for Company indemnity on ACA operational claims, or at minimum carve-outs from any basket for fundamental/control items.
- Basket must not apply to control failures or scheduled retained liabilities.

Counterparty deviation:
- Converts basket from deductible to tipping (once threshold exceeded, liability runs from first dollar).

Schedule interaction:
- Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities could be pulled into tipping mechanics if not carved out, altering economic allocation of scheduled items.

Risk rating: MEDIUM (client-conceded as to type); residual MEDIUM if carve-outs omitted

Exposure analysis:
- Tipping basket increases Company exposure once threshold crossed (first-dollar true-up) relative to a pure deductible — generally better for indemnified persons on quantum above the threshold, but can be paired with a reduced cap (Issue 1) as a trade that is still net-negative.
- Primary residual risk is not the tipping feature itself (client concedes) but failure to carve out Excluded Cap Claims / Schedule 5.2 / Article II control failures from the Basket.

Recommended position:
- CONCEDE tipping basket conversion per controlling deal-team instruction (latest partner email).
- CONDITION acceptance on: (i) restoration of cap (Issue 1); (ii) Basket inapplicable to Excluded Cap Claims, Section 5.2, Section 6.5, and Article II control failures; (iii) Basket amount no less favorable than playbook floor.
- Do not accept tipping basket as consideration for survival cut (Issue 4) or MAE carve-outs (Issue 3).

Redline treatment: INSERT tipping basket with express carve-outs (aca-redline.docx §6.3).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 3 — MAE Definition: Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Article I, Section 1.1 — definition of "Material Adverse Effect"; related Section 3.1(g) representation; Section 4.1(c) notice covenant.

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
- ACA MAE (or incorporation of Credit Agreement MAE) must not carve out regulatory actions/inquiries/investigations of the type that can impair deposit accounts, Bank compliance with Instructions, or Lien/control quality.
- Credit Agreement MAE does not contain the counterparty's proposed regulatory carve-outs; ACA should not create a more permissive MAE for Company escape hatches.

Counterparty deviation:
- Adds carve-outs excluding from MAE: (i) regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination or proceeding by any Governmental Authority; (ii) changes in law/regulation/regulatory policy (including banking, deposit-insurance, sanctions); (iii) public announcement or pendency of the foregoing.

Schedule interaction:
- Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect exactly these carve-outs. If carve-outs stand, material adverse developments in the scheduled inquiries could be argued to fall outside MAE, undermining termination, default, or covenant triggers that reference MAE, and weakening the utility of the new/related regulatory representation.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
- Off-market relative to Credit Agreement MAE and secured-party ACA practice where regulatory risk is live.
- Creates a documentation mismatch: schedules disclose the inquiries while the definition attempts to neutralize their MAE consequences.
- Could impair Secured Party leverage if regulatory developments threaten Account access, Bank cooperation, or collateral value.
- Change-in-law carve-out is especially broad in a banking/deposit-account context (sanctions, deposit insurance, bank resolution).

Recommended position:
- REJECT all three regulatory carve-outs in full; restore Credit Agreement-aligned MAE.
- INSERT Company representation Section 3.1(g) expressly qualified by Schedule 3.7 (pending inquiries disclosed; no other pending/threatened regulatory matters that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect Accounts, Bank compliance with Instructions, or Secured Party control/Lien).
- INSERT prompt-notice covenant for regulatory actions of that type (Section 4.1(c)).
- Do not trade MAE carve-outs for basket concession.

Redline treatment: DELETE proviso carve-outs to MAE; INSERT §3.1(g) and notice covenant; retain Schedule 3.7 (aca-redline.docx §§1.1, 3.1, 4.1, Schedule 3.7).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 4 — Survival / Limitation Period Shortened for Core Representations
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Article VIII, Section 8.3 (Survival); Exhibit B (Survival Matrix); Article III representations.

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
- Fundamental representations (account title/sole holder, Schedule I accuracy, no competing control agreement, Bank no-third-party-control rep) survive for periods no shorter than Credit Agreement fundamental-rep survival and Exhibit B matrix; indemnity survival is not collapsed into a short contractual limitation period.
- Exhibit B controls over body text.

Counterparty deviation:
- New limitation period shortens survival for core representations (e.g., to twelve (12) months or other shortened period in markup).

Schedule / exhibit interaction:
- Exhibit B sets the survival matrix the markup's limitation-period change contradicts.
- Scheduled exceptions control; Exhibit B is part of the operative package.

Risk rating: CRITICAL — WALK-AWAY

Exposure analysis:
- Short survival on fundamental control/title/no-competing-agreement reps creates a cliff after which the Secured Party may lack contractual remedy for latent defects in control perfection architecture.
- Direct contradiction of Exhibit B invites ambiguity and litigation over which provision controls.
- Client has designated any survival-period reduction a walk-away issue (controlling deal correspondence). Counsel must not "split the difference" by accepting a moderate shortening.

Recommended position:
- REJECT any shortening of survival for core representations — non-negotiable / walk-away.
- REINSTATE Exhibit B Survival Matrix by full insertion if omitted or altered; Section 8.3 must state Exhibit B controls over contrary body language.
- Survive indemnity without short contractual sunset (subject to statute of limitations), with Cap/Basket only as restored under Issues 1–2.
- Asserted claims before period end survive until final resolution.

Redline treatment: DELETE shortened limitation period; INSERT §8.3(a)–(e) and Exhibit B matrix (aca-redline.docx §8.3, Exhibit B).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 5 — Control Mechanics / NEOC Conditions (Bank-Form and Playbook Gaps)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Article II §§2.2–2.5; Article VII §7.2; Exhibit A.

Playbook / Bank form requirement:
- Irrevocable Bank agreement to comply with Secured Party Instructions without further Company consent (UCC §9-104).
- Commercially reasonable authentication only; no open-ended extra indemnity/conditions post-authentication.
- Prompt written confirmation of Control Notice and balances (playbook: within one Business Day).
- Anti-competing control agreement rep/covenant from Bank and Company.
- Schedule I update covenant; no offshore relocation of Accounts without consent.

Counterparty / draft gaps:
- Soft or missing confirmation timing; potential for Bank to layer conditions after NEOC; incomplete anti-competing-control covenant; incomplete Schedule I change control.

Risk rating: MEDIUM-HIGH (perfection and practical enforcement)

Exposure analysis:
- Delay or conditionality on NEOC undermines exclusive control when default remedies are needed.
- Competing control agreements destroy or prime "control" priority.
- Stale Schedule I impairs operational ability to issue effective Instructions.

Recommended position:
- INSERT one-Business-Day confirmation; bar on additional post-authentication conditions; Bank and Company anti-competing-control provisions; Schedule I update within three Business Days; US-location covenant.

Redline treatment: aca-redline.docx §§2.1–2.5, 3.2, 4.1–4.2, 7.2, Exhibit A.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 6 — Bank Setoff Breadth
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Article V §5.1.

Playbook requirement: Bank setoff limited to Account-related fees, returned items, chargebacks, overdrafts; no broad setoff for unrelated Company obligations to Bank; post-NEOC setoff restricted.

Counterparty / Bank paper tendency: Broad setoff/recoupment for any obligations of Company to Bank.

Risk rating: MEDIUM-HIGH

Exposure analysis: Broad setoff can drain controlled Accounts and prime or erode Secured Party's practical recovery at enforcement.

Recommended position: DELETE broad setoff; INSERT account-limited setoff and post-NEOC consent construct (with short returned-item tail).

Redline treatment: aca-redline.docx §5.1.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 7 — Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities — Silent Shift via Indemnity Mechanics
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Schedule 5.2; §§5.2, 6.2, 6.3.

Playbook / schedule rule: Scheduled retained liabilities remain with Company; indemnification cap/basket changes must not reallocate them to Secured Party.

Counterparty deviation: Cap cut + basket conversion without Schedule 5.2 carve-outs would silently shift economic exposure.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis: Secured Party could inherit residual exposure for items the disclosure package allocated to Company.

Recommended position: Express anti-shift language in §5.2; carve Schedule 5.2 from Cap and Basket; list schedule in Excluded Cap Claims.

Redline treatment: aca-redline.docx §§5.2, 6.2, 6.3, Schedule 5.2.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 8 — Governing Law / Venue Alignment
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: Article IX.

Playbook / Credit Agreement: New York law (including UCC Article 9) and Manhattan forum preferred; alignment with Credit Agreement reduces conflict-of-laws risk on control perfection narrative.

Risk rating: LOW-MEDIUM (if counterparty pushed Bank home state)

Recommended position: Maintain NY governing law and Manhattan exclusive venue; jury waiver retained.

Redline treatment: aca-redline.docx §9.1–9.3.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 9 — Missing Secured-Party-Favorable Boilerplate
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Items often thin on counterparty/Bank paper:
- Secured Party assignment without consent on Credit Agreement succession (§10.2)
- Lenders/Secured Parties as third-party beneficiaries (§10.4)
- ACA controls over deposit account agreement on control/priority/setoff/Instructions (§10.3)
- Further assurances including UCC filings if requested (§10.5)
- Force majeure not excusing NEOC compliance beyond short period (§10.6)
- Account statements to Secured Party on request (§4.2)

Risk rating: LOW-MEDIUM individually; MEDIUM in aggregate

Recommended position: Insert all per playbook; see redline Article IV, VII, X.

IV. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX

| # | Topic | Section(s) | Counterparty Position | Playbook / Base Requirement | Schedule / Exhibit Interaction | Client Instruction | Risk | Disposition | Recommended Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Indemnification Cap | §6.2 | Silent reduction of cap | Cap at CA/playbook level; uncapped fundamental/control buckets | Schedule 5.2 would be impaired by low cap | Protect economics | HIGH | REJECT | Restore cap + Excluded Cap Claims |
| 2 | Indemnification Basket | §6.3 | Convert deductible → tipping | Prefer deductible or carved tipping | Schedule 5.2 must be carved out | CONCEDE tipping | MED | CONCEDE w/ conditions | Accept tipping; carve Excluded Cap Claims / §5.2 / control |
| 3 | MAE regulatory carve-outs | §1.1 MAE | Carve out regulatory actions, change in law, pendency | No such carve-outs; align to Credit Agreement MAE | Schedule 3.7 two pending inquiries intersect carve-outs | Protect MAE | HIGH | REJECT | Delete carve-outs; add §3.1(g) + notice covenant |
| 4 | Survival / limitation period | §8.3; Ex. B | Shorten survival for core reps | Exhibit B matrix; CA fundamental floors | Exhibit B contradicted | WALK-AWAY if shortened | CRITICAL | REJECT | Reinstate Exhibit B; no shortening |
| 5 | NEOC / control mechanics | §§2.2–2.5, 7.2 | Soft timing/conditions; gaps | 1-BD confirm; no extra conditions; anti-compete control | Account details / Schedule I | Playbook floor | MED-HIGH | REQUIRE INSERTS | Insert timing, anti-compete, Schedule I updates |
| 6 | Bank setoff | §5.1 | Broad setoff for any Company obligations | Account-limited setoff; post-NEOC limits | Operational drain risk | Playbook floor | MED-HIGH | REJECT broad setoff | Narrow setoff + returned-item tail |
| 7 | Retained liabilities shift | Sch 5.2; §§5.2, 6.2–6.3 | Silent shift via cap/basket | Company retains Schedule 5.2 items | Schedule 5.2 controls | Protect allocation | HIGH | REJECT shift | Anti-shift language; carve from Cap/Basket |
| 8 | Governing law / venue | Art. IX | Possible Bank-state shift | NY law + Manhattan venue | Align to Credit Agreement | Standard | LOW-MED | REQUIRE NY | Keep NY + jury waiver |
| 9 | Boilerplate gaps | Arts. IV, VII, X | Missing TPB, assignment, supremacy, statements | Playbook secured-party set | — | Standard | LOW-MED | REQUIRE INSERTS | Insert full playbook set |

V. MISSING PROTECTIONS CHECKLIST (PLAYBOOK vs. COUNTERPARTY PAPER)

[ ] Irrevocable control agreement language (UCC §9-104) — reinforce if softened
[x] NEOC confirmation within 1 Business Day — INSERT
[x] No post-authentication conditions to honor Instructions — INSERT
[x] Bank representation: no other control agreement — retain/strengthen
[x] Bank covenant: no future competing control agreement without Secured Party consent — INSERT
[x] Company covenant: no competing control agreement / Lien — retain/strengthen
[x] Schedule I accuracy rep + 3-BD update covenant — INSERT
[x] Narrow Bank setoff — INSERT
[x] Schedule 5.2 anti-shift — INSERT
[x] Indemnity cap restored + Excluded Cap Claims — INSERT
[x] Basket tipping conceded with carve-outs — INSERT
[x] MAE without regulatory carve-outs — RESTORE
[x] Section 3.1(g) regulatory rep tied to Schedule 3.7 — INSERT
[x] Exhibit B survival matrix controlling — RESTORE (WALK-AWAY)
[x] NY governing law / Manhattan venue / jury waiver — RETAIN
[x] Secured Party assignment on CA succession — INSERT
[x] Secured Parties as third-party beneficiaries — INSERT
[x] ACA supremacy over deposit account agreement on control terms — INSERT
[x] Account statements to Secured Party — INSERT
[x] Force majeure limited as to NEOC — INSERT

VI. OFF-MARKET TERMS

1. Regulatory MAE carve-outs while Schedule 3.7 discloses live regulatory inquiries — off-market and internally inconsistent.
2. Silent indemnity cap reduction without reciprocal give — off-market relative to negotiated Credit Agreement economics.
3. Contractual shortening of fundamental-rep survival below Exhibit B / Credit Agreement floors — off-market for control agreements tied to a funded secured facility; client walk-away.
4. Broad Bank setoff against controlled accounts for unrelated exposures — common on Bank paper but off-market to secured-party playbook and should be resisted.

VII. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION PACKAGE

Give:
- Tipping basket (Issue 2), subject to carve-outs and no linkage to Issues 1, 3, or 4.
